t: Ranavalona III, the last sovereign ruler of the Kingdom of Madagascar, was deposed by French military forces.
British physicist J. J. Thomson and his team announce the discovery of the electron.
The Ramakrishna Mission was founded by Swami Vivekananda to serve as the humanitarian counterpart to the Hindu monastic order Ramakrishna Math.
The first Blackwall Tunnel under the River Thames was opened to improve commerce and trade in the East End of London.

The Church of England returned the original manuscript of William Bradford's Of Plymouth Plantation, an account of the Pilgrims and the early years of the Plymouth Colony, to the state of Massachusetts.
The Ancient Temples and Shrines Preservation Law was passed, instituting the protection of structures and artifacts in Japan designated National Treasures.
Mahdist War: Anglo-Egyptian soldiers clashed with Mahdist Sudanese rebels in the Battle of Abu Hamed.
The first meeting of the International Congress of Mathematicians was held in Zürich, Switzerland.
The Bersey Electric Cab entered service as the first electric taxi in London.
Thomas Edison was granted a patent for the Kinetoscope, a precursor to the modern movie projector.

Gaki Sherocho was captured by the forces of Ethiopian emperor Menelik II, bringing an end to the Kingdom of Kaffa.
In response to a letter written by eight-year-old Virginia O'Hanlon, The New York Sun published an editorial by Francis Pharcellus Church stating, "Yes, Virginia, there is a Santa Claus".
French actress, journalist and leading suffragette Marguerite Durand founded the feminist newspaper La Fronde.
